ESV.1: Then David said in his heart, “Now I shall perish one day by the hand of Saul. There is nothing better for me than that I should escape to the land of the Philistines. Then Saul will despair of seeking me any longer within the borders of Israel, and I shall escape out of his hand.”
ESV.2: So David arose and went over, he and the six hundred men who were with him, to Achish the son of Maoch, king of Gath.
ESV.3: And David lived with Achish at Gath, he and his men, every man with his household, and David with his two wives, Ahinoam of Jezreel, and Abigail of Carmel, Nabal's widow.
ESV.4: And when it was told Saul that David had fled to Gath, he no longer sought him.
ESV.5: Then David said to Achish, “If I have found favor in your eyes, let a place be given me in one of the country towns, that I may dwell there. For why should your servant dwell in the royal city with you?”
ESV.6: So that day Achish gave him Ziklag. Therefore Ziklag has belonged to the kings of Judah to this day.
ESV.7: And the number of the days that David lived in the country of the Philistines was a year and four months.
ESV.8: Now David and his men went up and made raids against the Geshurites, the Girzites, and the Amalekites, for these were the inhabitants of the land from of old, as far as Shur, to the land of Egypt.
ESV.9: And David would strike the land and would leave neither man nor woman alive, but would take away the sheep, the oxen, the donkeys, the camels, and the garments, and come back to Achish.
ESV.10: When Achish asked, “Where have you made a raid today?” David would say, “Against the Negeb of Judah,” or, “Against the Negeb of the Jerahmeelites,” or, “Against the Negeb of the Kenites.”
ESV.11: And David would leave neither man nor woman alive to bring news to Gath, thinking, “lest they should tell about us and say, ‘So David has done.’” Such was his custom all the while he lived in the country of the Philistines.
ESV.12: And Achish trusted David, thinking, “He has made himself an utter stench to his people Israel; therefore he shall always be my servant.”

NASB.1: Then David said to himself, 'Now I will perish one day by the hand of Saul. There is nothing better for me than to escape into the land of the Philistines. Saul then will despair of searching for me anymore in all the territory of Israel, and I will escape from his hand.'
NASB.2: So David arose and crossed over, he and the six hundred men who were with him, to Achish the son of Maoch, king of Gath.
NASB.3: And David lived with Achish at Gath, he and his men, each with his household, [even] David with his two wives, Ahinoam the Jezreelitess, and Abigail the Carmelitess, Nabal's widow.
NASB.4: Now it was told Saul that David had fled to Gath, so he no longer searched for him.
NASB.5: Then David said to Achish, 'If now I have found favor in your sight, let them give me a place in one of the cities in the country, that I may live there; for why should your servant live in the royal city with you?'
NASB.6: So Achish gave him Ziklag that day; therefore Ziklag has belonged to the kings of Judah to this day.
NASB.7: The number of days that David lived in the country of the Philistines was a year and four months.
NASB.8: Now David and his men went up and raided the Geshurites and the Girzites and the Amalekites; for they were the inhabitants of the land from ancient times, as you come to Shur even as far as the land of Egypt.
NASB.9: David attacked the land and did not leave a man or a woman alive, and he took away the sheep, the cattle, the donkeys, the camels, and the clothing. Then he returned and came to Achish.
NASB.10: Now Achish said, 'Where have you made a raid today?' And David said, 'Against the Negev of Judah and against the Negev of the Jerahmeelites and against the Negev of the Kenites.'
NASB.11: David did not leave a man or a woman alive to bring to Gath, saying, 'Otherwise they will tell about us, saying, 'So has David done and so [has been] his practice all the time he has lived in the country of the Philistines.''
NASB.12: So Achish believed David, saying, 'He has surely made himself odious among his people Israel; therefore he will become my servant forever.'

NLT.1: But David kept thinking to himself, “Someday Saul is going to get me. The best thing I can do is escape to the Philistines. Then Saul will stop hunting for me in Israelite territory, and I will finally be safe.”
NLT.2: So David took his 600 men and went over and joined Achish son of Maoch, the king of Gath.
NLT.3: David and his men and their families settled there with Achish at Gath. David brought his two wives along with him — Ahinoam from Jezreel and Abigail, Nabal’s widow from Carmel.
NLT.4: Word soon reached Saul that David had fled to Gath, so he stopped hunting for him.
NLT.5: One day David said to Achish, “If it is all right with you, we would rather live in one of the country towns instead of here in the royal city.”
NLT.6: So Achish gave him the town of Ziklag (which still belongs to the kings of Judah to this day),
NLT.7: and they lived there among the Philistines for a year and four months.
NLT.8: David and his men spent their time raiding the Geshurites, the Girzites, and the Amalekites — people who had lived near Shur, toward the land of Egypt, since ancient times.
NLT.9: David did not leave one person alive in the villages he attacked. He took the sheep, goats, cattle, donkeys, camels, and clothing before returning home to see King Achish.
NLT.10: “Where did you make your raid today?” Achish would ask. And David would reply, “Against the south of Judah, the Jerahmeelites, and the Kenites.”
NLT.11: No one was left alive to come to Gath and tell where he had really been. This happened again and again while he was living among the Philistines.
NLT.12: Achish believed David and thought to himself, “By now the people of Israel must hate him bitterly. Now he will have to stay here and serve me forever!”

CSB17.1: David said to himself, “One of these days I’ll be swept away by Saul. There is nothing better for me than to escape immediately to the land of the Philistines. <sup>ⓙ</sup> Then Saul will give up searching for me everywhere in Israel, and I’ll escape from him.”
CSB17.2: So David set out with his six hundred men <sup>ⓚ</sup> and went over to Achish son of Maoch, <sup>ⓛ</sup> the king of Gath.
CSB17.3: David and his men stayed with Achish in Gath. Each man had his family with him, <sup>ⓜ</sup> and David had his two wives: Ahinoam of Jezreel and Abigail of Carmel, <sup>ⓝ</sup> Nabal’s widow.
CSB17.4: When it was reported to Saul that David had fled to Gath, he no longer searched for him.
CSB17.5: Now David said to Achish, “If I have found favor with you, let me be given a place in one of the outlying towns, so I can live there. Why should your servant live in the royal city with you?”
CSB17.6: That day Achish gave Ziklag <sup>ⓐ</sup> to him, and it still belongs to the kings of Judah today.
CSB17.7: The length of time that David stayed in Philistine territory amounted to a year and four months. <sup>ⓑ</sup>
CSB17.8: David and his men went up and raided the Geshurites, <sup>ⓒ</sup> the Girzites, <sup>[1]</sup> and the Amalekites. <sup>ⓓ</sup> From ancient times they had been the inhabitants of the region through Shur <sup>ⓔ</sup> as far as the land of Egypt.
CSB17.9: Whenever David attacked the land, he did not leave a single person alive, either man or woman, but he took flocks, herds, donkeys, camels, and clothing. <sup>ⓕ</sup> Then he came back to Achish,
CSB17.10: who inquired, “Where did you raid today?” <sup>[2]</sup> <sup>ⓖ</sup> David replied, “The south country of Judah,” “The south country of the Jerahmeelites,” <sup>ⓗ</sup> or “The south country of the Kenites.” <sup>ⓘ</sup>
CSB17.11: David did not let a man or woman live to be brought to Gath, for he said, “Or they will inform on us and say, ‘This is what David did.’” This was David’s custom during the whole time he stayed in the Philistine territory.
CSB17.12: So Achish trusted David, thinking, “Since he has made himself repulsive to his people Israel, he will be my servant forever.”

MSG.1: David thought to himself, "Sooner or later, Saul's going to get me. The best thing I can do is escape to Philistine country. Saul will count me a lost cause and quit hunting me down in every nook and cranny of Israel. I'll be out of his reach for good."
MSG.2: So David left; he and his six hundred men went to Achish son of Maoch, king of Gath.
MSG.3: They moved in and settled down in Gath, with Achish. Each man brought his household; David brought his two wives, Ahinoam of Jezreel and Abigail, widow of Nabal of Carmel.
MSG.4: When Saul was told that David had escaped to Gath, he called off the hunt.
MSG.5: Then David said to Achish, "If it's agreeable to you, assign me a place in one of the rural villages. It doesn't seem right that I, your mere servant, should be taking up space in the royal city."
MSG.6: So Achish assigned him Ziklag. (This is how Ziklag got to be what it is now, a city of the kings of Judah.)
MSG.7: David lived in Philistine country a year and four months.
MSG.8: From time to time David and his men raided the Geshurites, the Girzites, and the Amalekites—these people were longtime inhabitants of the land stretching toward Shur and on to Egypt.
MSG.9: When David raided an area he left no one alive, neither man nor woman, but took everything else: sheep, cattle, donkeys, camels, clothing—the works. Then he'd return to Achish.
MSG.10:
Achish would ask, "And whom did you raid today?"
David would tell him, "Oh, the Negev of Judah," or "The Negev of Jerahmeel," or "The Negev of the Kenites."
MSG.11: He never left a single person alive lest one show up in Gath and report what David had really been doing. This is the way David operated all the time he lived in Philistine country.
MSG.12: Achish came to trust David completely. He thought, "He's made himself so repugnant to his people that he'll be in my camp forever."

NIV.1:
David Among the Philistines
But David thought to himself, “One of these days I will be destroyed by the hand of Saul. The best thing I can do is to escape to the land of the Philistines. Then Saul will give up searching for me anywhere in Israel, and I will slip out of his hand.”
NIV.2: So David and the six hundred men with him left and went over to Achish son of Maoch king of Gath.
NIV.3: David and his men settled in Gath with Achish. Each man had his family with him, and David had his two wives: Ahinoam of Jezreel and Abigail of Carmel, the widow of Nabal.
NIV.4: When Saul was told that David had fled to Gath, he no longer searched for him.
NIV.5: Then David said to Achish, “If I have found favor in your eyes, let a place be assigned to me in one of the country towns, that I may live there. Why should your servant live in the royal city with you?”
NIV.6: So on that day Achish gave him Ziklag, and it has belonged to the kings of Judah ever since.
NIV.7: David lived in Philistine territory a year and four months.
NIV.8: Now David and his men went up and raided the Geshurites, the Girzites and the Amalekites. (From ancient times these peoples had lived in the land extending to Shur and Egypt.)
NIV.9: Whenever David attacked an area, he did not leave a man or woman alive, but took sheep and cattle, donkeys and camels, and clothes. Then he returned to Achish.
NIV.10: When Achish asked, “Where did you go raiding today?” David would say, “Against the Negev of Judah” or “Against the Negev of Jerahmeel” or “Against the Negev of the Kenites.”
NIV.11: He did not leave a man or woman alive to be brought to Gath, for he thought, “They might inform on us and say, ‘This is what David did.’” And such was his practice as long as he lived in Philistine territory.
NIV.12: Achish trusted David and said to himself, “He has become so odious to his people, the Israelites, that he will be my servant forever.”

NET.2: So David left and crossed over to King Achish son of Maoch of Gath accompanied by his six hundred men.

NET.8: Then David and his men went up and raided the Geshurites, the Girzites, and the Amalekites. (They had been living in that land for a long time, from the approach to Shur as far as the land of Egypt.)
NET.9: When David would attack a district, he would leave neither man nor woman alive. He would take sheep, cattle, donkeys, camels, and clothing and would then go back to Achish.
NET.10: When Achish would ask, “Where did you raid today?” David would say, “The Negev of Judah” or “The Negev of Jeharmeel” or “The Negev of the Kenites.”
NET.11: Neither man nor woman would David leave alive so as to bring them back to Gath. He was thinking, “This way they can’t tell on us, saying, ‘This is what David did.’” Such was his practice the entire time that he lived in the country of the Philistines.
NET.12: So Achish trusted David, thinking to himself, “He is really hated among his own people in Israel! From now on he will be my servant.”
